requirements.text: Review the forwarded GPT code-graph pilot proposal and determine whether it is a good fit for the NYC Buildability program.
Identify potential issues/conflicts between the proposal and work already completed (control plane, directives, hooks, worktrees, policies, accepted tasks, active lanes).

Determine how the proposal would be implemented and run within the current execution environment (Windows 11 thin client, PowerShell 5.1 primary plus Git Bash, protected-main workflow, CI-heavy execution).

Check the proposal against the recently implemented security controls (dependency-security/age-gate policy, hook guards, permission posture, secret scanning) and identify any security issues or required adjustments.
Assess whether a better/easier approach achieves the same navigation goal; compare alternatives before recommending.
Decide and state the recommended next step; implementation proceeds on the basis of that recommendation.

requirements.text: Prefer an isolated tool environment such as uv tool/pipx rather than contaminating the repository Python environment.
Record the pilot provenance facts.
First extraction is CODE ONLY where practical; the first question is whether deterministic/local AST-based code graphing materially improves navigation of this repository.
Do not feed sensitive content into an external model.
Where Graphify allows local tree-sitter extraction, prefer that mode; do not enable optional model/API processing merely because it exists.
Generate the normal graph artifacts in the isolated pilot (e.g. graph.json / graph.html / human-readable report), inspecting current Graphify behavior rather than assuming exact filenames.
Before benchmarking, inspect whether the graph actually understands this repository across all 16 Part-6 dimensions.

checklist.text: whether dynamic Python/TypeScript behavior creates blind spots

requirements.text: Produce concrete examples of GOOD graph relationships and of WRONG or MISSING graph relationships; do not claim accuracy because graph.html looks impressive.

Create a small reproducible navigation benchmark of approximately 15-25 questions representative of real NYC Buildability work, adapted to current repository architecture rather than blindly reusing the example names.

For each benchmark question run APPROACH A (baseline: normal Claude repository navigation via the existing approved workflow) measuring where practical: elapsed time, searches, grep/glob calls, source files opened, approximate retrieved/context volume, correctness, completeness, mistaken detours.

For each benchmark question run APPROACH B (graph first: use graph output/query mechanisms to identify relevant nodes/paths/files, then verify important conclusions against actual source code) measuring: elapsed time, graph queries, source files opened, approximate retrieved/context volume, correctness, completeness, mistaken graph paths.

Produce the per-question comparison table with the Part-8 columns (question; baseline result; graph-first result; correct?; complete?; files opened; navigation steps/tool calls; graph missed anything?; graph invented anything?; source verification required?; winner).
Produce the overall scoring.
Do NOT invent precise token savings if tokens cannot actually be measured; use observable measures instead.

Trust model: the code graph must NEVER become authoritative truth. Canonical truth remains Git content, actual source files, project-control, schemas/contracts, CI, and accepted gate evidence. The graph is an INDEX / NAVIGATION PROJECTION.

Enforce the required pattern (TASK -> GRAPH QUERY -> LIKELY FILES/CALL PATH -> READ AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE -> IMPLEMENT/REVIEW) and forbid the pattern (TASK -> GRAPH -> TRUST WITHOUT SOURCE VERIFICATION).
Define which kinds of graph results require source verification; at minimum anything involving the listed categories must still be confirmed from authoritative source.
Design (not necessarily implement yet) a deterministic graph-freshness model whose metadata records the listed facts.

Freshness rule: before an agent uses the graph, compare graph_source_sha vs the current working/frozen task SHA; if they differ, STATE = STALE, and stale graph information must not be presented as current.
For active task worktrees, think carefully about whether graphing origin/main, the frozen task base, or the task HEAD is appropriate; do not assume one answer fits every lifecycle stage.
Evaluate Graphify's incremental-update capability and design the safest initial refresh pattern (session/task start -> check graph metadata -> query if current, controlled update if not -> continue).
Do NOT automatically install Git hooks yet; especially do not add commit/push hooks while the existing hook/confinement work is still sensitive, unless separately reviewed and owner-authorized.
Later update automation may only be PROPOSED in this evaluation, not enacted.

If the pilot succeeds, propose how graph-first navigation should integrate with the existing context-routing approach (controlled task -> minimal task/control capsule -> relevant graph neighborhood -> subsystem/files/dependencies -> read authoritative source files only -> implement).
Do NOT force the full graph.json into Claude's context; graph retrieval must be targeted.
Design targeted graph query patterns.
Evaluate how a graph could help Agent Teams (orchestrator scopes the task; each teammate receives only its relevant graph neighborhood).
Do NOT change the current agent confinement model during this pilot; the graph must not be used as justification to loosen safety controls.
Evaluate whether parallel agents could safely share one graph artifact read-only.

Produce a design note (do NOT implement now) for eventually adding project-control relationships to a graph projection using the Part-14 node types (task, directive, requirement, blocker, milestone, gate, PR, product system, file, module, contract) and edge types (IMPLEMENTS, PART_OF, DEPENDS_ON, BLOCKED_BY, MODIFIES, DELIVERS, REVIEWS, CONSUMED_BY). That projection must be GENERATED FROM canonical project-control/Git sources and must not become a competing manually edited source of truth.

Evaluate (recommendation only; do not build unless separately authorized) whether the owner Mission-Control dashboard could later add an ENGINEERING MAP / CODE MAP view (owner view: purpose, engineering %, launch readiness, blockers; technical view: modules, key files, key contracts, upstream dependencies, downstream consumers) reusing graph output rather than duplicating architecture metadata.

Record explicitly that Graphify/code graphing is NOT the future NYC evidence graph; that future system (properties, BBL/BIN, districts, rules, sources, filings, plans, benchmark cases, solver runs, discrepancies, etc.) needs its own data model/provenance/temporal semantics, and Graphify must not become the canonical data store for those.
STOP and return to the owner before adoption if any Part-17 stop condition occurs; never work around a STOP condition silently.
